primitives.name: Portable Inference Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision A cross-platform, high-performance inference accelerator for ML models: train in any framework (PyTorch, sklearn, LightGBM, XGBoost — all export to ONNX), serve with one runtime on any hardware (CPU, CUDA, TensorRT, CoreML, DirectML, OpenVINO via *execution providers*).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M': 'model artifact (dimensionless)', 'R': 'runtime environment (CPU, CUDA, etc.)', 'F': 'framework (PyTorch, sklearn, etc.)'}
primitives.assumptions: Model artifacts are convertible to ONNX format; runtime supports target execution provider.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model export fails or execution provider is unsupported.

layer2.mapping: ONNX Runtime maps model abstraction M across frameworks F to runtime R, preserving functional equivalence under different hardware configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Validation set parity between original and ONNX-represented model.

primitives.name: Execution Provider Abstraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Execution providers are pluggable — same ONNX file, CPU today, CUDA/TensorRT tomorrow, with no model change.
primitives.assumptions: Same ONNX model O can be executed under E without modification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E does not support all operations in O.

layer2.mapping: Execution provider E acts as a kernel that interprets ONNX model O in a specific compute context, enabling dynamic scaling of inference resources.
layer2.telemetry: Runtime performance metrics under varying E configurations.

primitives.name: Quantized Inference Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Quantization toolchain included:** ONNX Runtime ships quantization tools (dynamic/static quantization, QDQ).
primitives.assumptions: Quantization preserves model accuracy within acceptable tolerance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When quantization introduces significant loss of fidelity.

layer2.mapping: Quantization engine Q transforms floating-point inputs I into lower-precision P representations, optimizing memory and latency while maintaining inference integrity.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy drop vs. latency improvement trade-off during quantization.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of ONNX Runtime is that model portability and runtime simplicity form a duality: models are exported once to ONNX, then served through a consistent runtime interface regardless of backend hardware. This aligns with GSE’s need for adaptable, low-latency inference. The execution provider abstraction allows switching between CPU and GPU inference without retraining, enabling state transitions in real-time event processing. The quantization toolchain ensures efficient deployment under resource constraints. Failure modes include export inconsistencies and unsupported ops, which are mitigated by round-trip validation and explicit testing. The MIT license and 22K+ stars validate its reliability and adoption in production systems.
